Definition: probably from δρύς (an oak); a tree:--tree.
BiblicalUsage: A tree in the Gospels is never just scenery; it is a picture of what a life produces. A good tree bears good fruit and a corrupt tree evil fruit, the mustard seed grows into a tree that shelters birds, and in Revelation the trees of the earth are spared until God's servants are sealed.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Jesus chose the tree because fruit cannot lie. What grows out of a life tells the truth about its root, and that is why He calls us to judge teaching by its fruit and to abide until our own lives bear His.
RelatedTopics: Fruit of the Spirit; Kingdom of God; Judgment
